findings.excerpt: The source opens a fenced block as ```tikzpicture, then has a bare \node command and closes with ```; the renderer prints \node[draw,circle] (v) {$1$}; literally.
findings.symptom: The one-vertex zero-arrow quiver diagram is printed as literal TikZ source in the Statement; it does not become a diagram.
findings.mathematical_check: The intended picture is a single vertex labelled 1 with no arrows, matching the stated one-vertex zero-arrow quiver. No mathematical map or orientation is at issue; the malformed fence prevents rendering.
findings.suggested_repair: Use a recognized ```tikz fence, put \begin{tikzpicture} on the next line, and retain the single circle node labelled 1.

findings.excerpt: Mathematical expressions in the proof are enclosed in backticks as code, for example `T(U,V)=U⊗V` and `m sigma=id_K`, and the screenshot displays the TeX-like strings as plain monospace ASCII.
findings.symptom: Proof formulas and object maps appear as literal code/text rather than formatted mathematics in the only screenshot tile.
findings.mathematical_check: This is a presentation defect in the source markup. The visible formula for the strong tensorator t_{(U,V),(U\prime,V\prime)} has the crossing c_{V,U\prime} and maps VU\prime to U\prime V; the subsequent candidate section expands with c_{B,A}^{-1}, consistent with the statement’s displayed separability section. Visual review did not find a sign/orientation reversal in those written formulas.
findings.suggested_repair: Replace backtick-delimited math expressions in proof lines 41–47 with the renderer’s math delimiters; keep code ticks only for actual code.
